name: Value-and-Structure Alignment for Routing-Consistent Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models
problem: MoE quantization error is amplified discontinuously: a tiny perturbation can flip the top-k expert choice, changing the entire computation path for that token.
mechanism: A PTQ OBJECTIVE (not an architecture change) that penalizes divergence of post-quantization expert selection from pre-quantization selection, in two complementary terms: VALUE alignment matches the routing-relevant logits/scores themselves, and STRUCTURE alignment preserves expert ORDERING and the top-k decision boundaries. Unlike methods that quantize routing scores directly, VSRAQ adds no inference-time overhead and plugs into existing quantization frameworks.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): 'unlike dense models, MoE models are sensitive to routing instability', and preserving routing consistency 'reduces quantization-induced degradation without introducing any inference-time overhead'. No numeric accuracy or compression figure in the abstract, so speedup_reported stays null. The zero-inference-overhead property is what separates it from EAQuant's routing-consistency penalty, which alters the objective during calibration but is also inference-free - the real difference is the loss form.
